newsitem.title: USA: U.S. power output falls 2.7 pct vs. year ago--EEI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. power output falls 2.7 pct vs. year ago--EEI.

text.p: Electricity deliveries in the continental U.S. totaled 60,388 gigawatt hours (GWh) for the week ended March 8, down 2.7 percent from the same period in 1996, the Edison Electric Institute (EEI) said Wednesday.
The amount of weekly power supplied to the New England area showed the largest year-to-year drop, falling 8.6 percent to 2,233 GWh, EEI said.
The Rocky Mountain region experienced the sharpest increase in power output, rising 5.6 percent from the corresponding period a year earlier to 2,961 GWh.
Year-to-date domestic power production for the first ten weeks of 1997 totaled 639,371 GWh, virtually unchanged from the same period in 1996, EEI said.
